citation: Kaslow and Madni (2017), Validation and Verification of MBSE-compliant CubeSat Reference Model
title: Validation and Verification of MBSE-compliant CubeSat Reference Model
venue_type: conference, 15th Annual Conference on Systems Engineering Research (CSER)
modeling_scope: System-level CubeSat Reference Model for a generic CubeSat mission domain. Scope includes domain/enterprise, space and ground segments, logical subsystem architecture including a high-level Power Subsystem, requirements/use-case/technical-measure traceability, logical-to-physical architecture development, behaviors, structures, validation and verification packages, mission-specific customization workflow, and mission modeling/V&V scenarios. EPS is represented only as a logical power subsystem, not as a detailed EPS behavioral model.
mbse_language_method_tool: MBSE using SysML and Object-Oriented Systems Engineering Methodology (OOSEM); CubeSat Reference Model as an OMG-oriented specification/reference model; modeling tool and COTS modeling/simulation tools are mentioned but not named.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite platform; CubeSat described as a low-cost standardized nanosatellite, basic 1U unit 10x10x10 cm and about 1.3 kg, with 1U/2U/3U common configurations; model targets university CubeSat teams and mission-specific CubeSat projects.
task_domain: Generic CubeSat mission analysis, design, development, deployment, and operations across space and ground segments; mission-specific CubeSat model derivation from a reference model.
interface: Model interfaces include stakeholder viewpoints, requirements traceability, space/ground segment and subsystem relationships, Ground Station Services and Transport/Launch/Deploy Services, spacecraft-ground communications, and model-to-tool integration with unnamed COTS modeling tools for mission scenario execution.
feedback: Technical measures are modeled as measurable block value properties that can be compared with target values. V&V workflow uses viewpoints as objective evidence, a CRM populated with a representative mission for verification, and mission modeling/V&V scenarios linked to validation and verification activities.
evaluation: The paper demonstrates the CRM concept through SysML-style views/figures of the CubeSat domain, space and ground segments, requirements hierarchy, mission-specific development flow, and V&V workflow. It proposes validation/verification through viewpoints, representative-mission population, independent review for SysML compliance, and mission modeling scenarios; it does not report empirical test metrics or a completed mission-specific evaluation.
rq_relevance: RQ1: partial because the paper gives a general MBSE/SysML CubeSat mission reference model and includes a high-level Power Subsystem, but it does not develop detailed EPS behavior. RQ2: partial because it claims modeling outcomes such as design/V&V facilitation, customization, reuse, communication, and efficiency/productivity; reliability is represented as a requirement/traceability concern rather than an achieved reliability outcome, and reproducibility/integrability are not empirically measured. RQ3: partial because validation and verification are central and integrated into the CRM through viewpoints, packages, representative missions, and V&V scenarios, but the procedures are system/model-level rather than EPS-specific.
claimed_outcomes: The CRM is intended to facilitate CubeSat design, verification, and validation.
The CRM is intended to support customization for specific CubeSat missions by mission-specific teams.
Providing a standard Reference Model with MBSE, OOSEM, and SysML is claimed to boost efficiency and productivity of less experienced teams without negative impacts.
A reference model is claimed to foster clear communications within collaborative stakeholder teams through an interlinked set of concepts.
CRM logical elements are intended for reuse as the starting point for mission-specific logical architecture and later physical architecture.

Reliability can be represented as a non-functional requirement and traced to lower-level requirements such as redundancy management, but no reliability improvement is measured or claimed as demonstrated.
Mission scenario execution and interface with COTS modeling tools are claimed as possible for V&V scenarios, but tool identities and integration performance are not reported.
verification_validation_linkage: Strong general V&V linkage. The CRM contains validation and verification packages; mission-specific teams develop a validation and verification approach; validation and verification are defined using objective evidence, with verification methods including inspection, analysis, demonstration, and test. CRM validation uses viewpoints; CRM verification uses viewpoints after populating the CRM with a representative mission; mission-specific models and CubeSats use viewpoints and V&V scenarios supported by mission modeling. No EPS-specific verification procedure is described.
key_findings: The CubeSat Reference Model is a generic MBSE/SysML reference model for the CubeSat mission domain, intended as a starting point for mission-specific CubeSat teams.

The CRM models CubeSat mission enterprise context, stakeholders, external environment, external constraints, space segment, ground segment, and services such as ground station and transport/launch/deploy services.

The space segment logical architecture decomposes the CubeSat into subsystems including Mission Payload, Communication, Command and Data Handling, Attitude Determination and Control, Guidance/Navigation/Control, Structures and Mechanisms, Power, Thermal, and Propulsion.
The Power Subsystem is only defined at a high level as generating, regulating, storing, and distributing power to the spacecraft.

Requirements are organized across enterprise, segment, and subsystem packages and traced to mission needs, objectives, constraints, use cases, measures of effectiveness, measures of performance, and technical performance measures.

Mission-specific model development is presented as populating CRM mission needs/objectives/constraints/measures, creating mission-specific logical architecture, then developing physical architecture and mission design.
V&V is integrated through model packages and viewpoints, with representative mission population for CRM verification and V&V scenarios/mission modeling for mission-specific models and CubeSats.

The paper does not provide detailed EPS behavioral modeling, EPS-specific verification procedures, quantitative evaluation results, or empirical evidence of reliability/reproducibility/integrability improvements.
limitations_gaps: Further research is needed into how to augment the CRM with other models for CubeSat test and evaluation.
The paper states challenges including no agreed-upon process for developing a CubeSat Enterprise and that no mission-specific CubeSat Enterprise had been modeled to date.
The CRM assumes users have intermediate-level understanding of space mission analysis and design, MBSE, and SysML, guided by subject matter experts.
The CRM is described as at least three levels of abstraction away from physical instantiation, so it does not provide a detailed physical EPS design.
Budget constraints and varying team skill/experience are identified as continuing challenges.
No formal threats-to-validity section or quantitative validation results are reported.

quality.rationale: Published as a conference paper in the 15th Annual Conference on Systems Engineering Research. The paper discusses challenges, assumptions, abstraction limits, and future research needs, but does not include a formal limitations or threats-to-validity section.
